deep.reconstruction:
Setting (consistent with the neighbouring pages). The objects are simple ('stable') arrangements of pseudolines. A projective simple arrangement (X, Σ = (D_i)_{i ∈ I_0 ⊔ {i_0}}) with a distinguished line Δ = D_{i_0} is the same thing as an affine (Euclidean) simple arrangement of n = card I_0 pseudolines. C_aff(n) is the set of isomorphism classes of such triples (X, Σ, Δ). The order in which the n lines meet Δ gives I_0 a polygonal (dihedral, cyclic-up-to-reversal) structure. C^!_aff st(I_0) consists of the labelled classes compatible with a fixed polygonal structure on I_0. The dihedral group D_{I_0}, of order 2n, acts on this set with quotient C_aff(n).

Step 1 (top of page; orbit–stabilizer). By the previous page, the stabilizer of a lift ξ is Aut(X, Σ, Δ). Hence card (α^!)^{-1}(ξ^q) = |D_{I_0}| / |G_ξ| = 2n / N(ξ), where N(ξ) = card Aut(X, Σ, Δ).

Step 2. Remove Δ and compactify the affine part to a disc. The 2n ends of the n pseudolines lie on the boundary circle and form a combinatorial 2n-gon S, with antipodal involution ±1_S and I_0 = S/{±1_S}. C̃_st(S) is the set of isotopy classes of discs carrying a stable system of curves pinned at S. In modern terms these are pinned wiring diagrams, i.e. commutation classes of reduced words of the longest element w_0 ∈ S_n, i.e. rhombic tilings of a 2n-gon, i.e. elements of the higher Bruhat order B(n,2).

Step 3. The forgetful map C̃_st(S) → C^!_aff st(I_0) has degree 2: one forgets which end of each line is which, the difference being the antipodal symmetry -1_S. The dihedral group D_S has order 4n. Composing, the composite map α̃ : C̃_st(S) → C_aff(n) ≅ C̃_st(S)/D_S has fibres of size 4n / N(ξ^q).

Summing over classes gives the mass formula card C̃_st(S) = Σ_{ξ ∈ C_aff(n)} 4n / N(ξ).

Example n = 3. There is a single class (the triangle), with Aut ≅ S_3 of order 6. So C̃_st(S) has 12/6 = 2 elements: the two resolutions of a triple point, i.e. the two reduced words of w_0 in S_3.

The next page treats n = 4: Aut = Z/2, giving 8 elements, which is indeed the number of commutation classes for S_4. It then starts n = 5 with 6 classes; the total should be 62. Purpose: enumerating and organizing simple pseudoline arrangements via the action of the dihedral symmetry of the boundary polygon.
errors: In Ex. 1 the orbit is said to be 'sous D_{I_0}'. The order-12 group acting on C̃_st(S) is D_S, of order 4n = 12, not D_{I_0} (order 6). The next page correctly writes D_S.

The degree-2 claim for C̃_st(S) → C^!(I_0) is asserted without justification. It needs -1_S to act freely on pinned classes. This holds for n ≥ 3: a centrally symmetric pinned stable system would force all lines through the fixed point, contradicting simplicity. Grothendieck does not argue this.
Stabilizer identification 'G_ξ ≅ Aut(X, Σ, Δ)' in D_{I_0} versus D_S (factor 2 bookkeeping) is used heuristically ('sans doute' on the previous page). The numbers check for n = 3, 4.

ideas.what: Orbit–stabilizer count of labelled/pinned affine simple pseudoline arrangements under the dihedral group, with stabilizer = automorphism group of the projective arrangement fixing the line at infinity
ideas.modern_name: Mass formula Σ 4n/|Aut| for commutation classes of reduced words of w_0 (rhombic tilings / B(n,2)) versus isomorphism classes of Euclidean simple arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ~1980–84); Knuth 'Axioms and Hulls' (1992) enumerations; Felsner and others

ideas.what: Discs with a stable system of curves pinned by a combinatorial 2n-gon S, with D_S action and quotient by ±1_S
ideas.modern_name: Pinned wiring diagrams / commutation classes of reduced decompositions of w_0 / rhombic tilings of the 2n-gon / higher Bruhat order B(n,2)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's isotopy classes of pinned discs C̃_st(S) are exactly Manin–Schechtman's B(n,2), i.e. commutation classes of reduced words of w_0. His counts 2, 8 (and presumably 62 for n = 5) match. He organizes them by the dihedral group of order 4n, with stabilizers equal to Aut of the projective arrangement fixing a line. This is several years before Manin–Schechtman's work, in a parallel 'isotopic category' language.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: an independent early appearance of the dihedral-symmetry viewpoint on B(n,2)/rhombic tilings. The mathematics itself is known/routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct orbit-counting formula, in Grothendieck's own language, for objects that are now standard (commutation classes / rhombic tilings). It is historically interesting as early independent work, but not new mathematically.
transcription_corrections: 'C^!_{diffst}(I_0)' and 'C_{·diff}(n)' are most likely Grothendieck's abbreviated 'C^!_{aff st}(I_0)' and 'C_{aff}(n)', as on the previous page; 'diff' is a misreading.
In Ex. 1 the manuscript reads 'consiste en une seule orbite sous D_{I_0}, d'ordre 12/6 = 2'. 'D_{I_0}' is Grothendieck's slip for D_S.
In the first displayed formula, the struck-out symbol before N(ξ) is an aborted N, and the result reads 2n/N(ξ).
